learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected louder than one speaker and locked the prediction for equal speakers with a half-wavelength path difference.
observations.exploration: At equal paths the sum was twice one speaker's wave height. Moved listener to 0.69 m right, giving a quarter-wave path difference and 1.4 times height. At 1.44 m right, half-wave difference, the sum was zero. At 3.61 m right, a whole-wave difference restored twice the height.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to almost nothing, accurately referred to cancellation at half a wave and restoration at a whole wave, and explained crest meeting trough. It disclosed equal source loudness and no echoes, distinguishing ideal cancellation from a real room's quiet spot.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot at the half-wave setting. Opposed orange and grey waveforms sat above a flat A+B line. The lower diagram showed circular crest and trough paths from two sources to the listener, with the 0.50 m difference and zero sum readouts.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question challenges simply adding the loudness of two sources.
prediction.evidence: Selected louder before exploring the half-wave condition.

interaction.reason: Listener positions reveal partial addition, cancellation and periodic restoration.
interaction.evidence: Quarter, half and full wavelength differences gave 1.4, zero and two times wave height.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the phase relationship and references the tested full-wave return.
payoff.evidence: Crest-trough cancellation and whole-wave alignment are both described.

clarity.reason: The waveform sum connects the spatial path difference to the local result.
clarity.evidence: The half-wave screenshot shows a flat A+B line and zero readout.

transfer.reason: The interference rule is explained without a new device or application.
transfer.evidence: All tested cases remain the same two speaker geometry.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Adding an identical source can make a location quieter.
surprise.evidence: The half-wave setting reduced the summed wave height to zero.

visualExplanation.reason: Spatial paths and local waveforms jointly expose cause and outcome across contrasts.
visualExplanation.evidence: The half-wave diagram aligns opposing waves; the full-wave case restores the sum.

playfulness.reason: Walking through constructive and destructive positions is a compact exploratory puzzle.
playfulness.evidence: The discrete listener slider reaches both a null and a renewed maximum.

practicalValue.reason: It explains why sound varies across locations near coherent speakers.
practicalValue.evidence: The real-room caveat qualifies the ideal silence.

depth.reason: The lesson includes the periodic return and idealization limits.
depth.evidence: A full wavelength restores alignment, with equal loudness and no echoes assumed.

complexity.reason: One position control is simple, while connecting distance, phase and amplitude is conceptually new.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: combine two wave heights based on relative timing.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: A longer path can oppose rather than merely delay an additive signal.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Wavelength, crest, trough and phase cancellation are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: circular wavefronts, two waveforms, a sum line and fractional wavelengths.

whyCool: Walking sideways turns the same two speakers from reinforcement to cancellation and back again.
caveat: The model assumes equal amplitude and no echoes. I inspected the visual wave sum; no audio listening was performed.
missingEvidence: No audio output or fresh source geometry was tested.
